notes: Rotate a page that was scanned sideways: a new Rotate button in the sidebar turns the page you are looking at a quarter turn each time you tap it, and brings it back upright on the fourth, so you can just tap until it looks right. Nothing is written to the PDF itself (exactly like Crop and Deskew), so it can never damage the original, and anything you have already written on the page turns with it and stays on the notes it belongs to; if you have two tablets paired, the rotation reaches the second one. Switch a piece off in a setlist: every piece in a playlist now has a tick box in front of it, and unticking it greys the name out and makes page-turning go straight past it - useful when a service list is mostly right but you are not playing one of the items today. The piece stays in the list so you can put it back with another tap, and the tick boxes are in both the Library's playlist editor and the list you get by holding a playlist tab in the reader. Start a setlist item part-way in: each piece in a playlist can be given a starting page, and for a hymnal you can enter the hymn number instead, so the list reads 'Hymn 342' rather than a page number - and because it is saved on the setlist rather than on the piece, one hymnal can appear in a service several times opening at a different hymn each time. Finally, the Library's menu is now a grid of icons with the name under each instead of a list of text, which should be quicker to find things in. Your library, annotations and licence are not affected.
